independence_evidence: The about page describes LOST as made by a small publishing studio (volume press, volume-press.com) that also produces other publications; the shop lists LOST and 'volume press' as vendors; no media group involvement.
qualifies_reason: Independent annual bilingual travel magazine whose Issue Eleven was published in October 2025 and is on sale in the publisher's shop.
what_it_is: A bilingual English and Chinese travel magazine built around first-person stories of self-discovery rather than destination guides, with roughly ten long personal narratives per issue plus commissioned photography. It appears once a year as a thick, uncoated-paper volume. It suits readers who like slow, reflective travel writing and Chinese-language perspectives on travel.

cover_candidates.notes: Flat front cover from magCulture. The publisher's own images (lostmagazine.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/LOST-Eleven-photos-1.jpg and the shop's LOST-Eleven-photos-crop.jpg, 1800x1260) are landscape product photographs rather than flat covers.

uncertainties: lostmagazine.org resets direct connections, so it was read through a fetch proxy; the shop (Shopify) was read directly. Neither the magazine site, the shop nor volume-press.com states a city or country: the shop trades in SGD with +08:00 timestamps and its stockist list begins with Singapore, while magCulture gives 'Shanghai, China and Singapore', so country and city are left null rather than guessed. Publisher legal name not stated; 'volume press' is the studio named on the about page. The distributor hint (Ra & Olly 2026-07) matches Issue Eleven, which the publisher dates 8 October 2025; cadence (Ten July 2024, Eleven Oct 2025) and the about page both indicate once a year.
